title: Parmigiana With a Dark Heart
description: A richly layered aubergine parmigiana built on San Marzano tomato, garlic, thyme and basil, with a hidden centre of sun-dried tomato and Halen Môn oak smoke — then a restrained flash of Maldon smoked sea salt at the table.

items.name: Plain flour, for the lightest dusting
Groundnut or sunflower oil, for shallow-frying
Tins whole peeled San Marzano tomatoes, including juice
Garlic cloves, finely sliced or chopped
Dried chilli flakes (up to ½ tsp if wanted)
Fine sea salt and freshly ground black pepper
Good vegetarian Italian-style hard cheese, finely grated
Fresh basil leaves, a large handful
Finished tomato sauce (taken from the batch above)

steps.title: Drain the mozzarella
steps.body: Tear or slice the mozzarella and place it in a sieve over a bowl for 45-60 minutes. Pat thoroughly dry before assembling. This is one of the main controls against a watery parmigiana.

steps.title: Salt the aubergines
steps.body: While the mozzarella drains, slice the aubergines lengthways about 5-6 mm thick. Salt lightly and leave in a colander for 25-30 minutes, then pat very thoroughly dry.

steps.title: Start the master tomato sauce
steps.body: Hand-crush the San Marzano tomatoes, keeping some small pieces rather than making them completely smooth. Warm the EVOO over low-medium heat. Add the onion and a small pinch of salt; cook gently for 8-10 minutes until soft and sweet without significant browning. Add the garlic and chilli and cook for 1-2 minutes, just until fragrant. Add the San Marzano tomatoes and juice, passata, thyme, basil stalks and the cheese rind if using. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook uncovered for about 45-60 minutes, stirring occasionally. Once the sauce is simmering, start frying the aubergines — do not wait for the sauce to finish.

steps.title: Fry the aubergines
steps.body: Dust the dried aubergine slices very lightly with flour, shaking off virtually all excess. Heat about 5-8 mm neutral oil in a broad frying pan. Fry in batches for about 1-2 minutes per side, until deeply golden, completely tender and lightly caramelised at the edges. Allow roughly 30-40 minutes for the full quantity. Drain extremely well on kitchen paper or, preferably, a rack over a tray.

steps.title: Finish and divide the sauce
steps.body: When the sauce is thick and spoonable, remove the thyme, basil stalks and rind. Do not reduce simply to hit a numerical yield: consistency matters more. Measure what you actually have. First set aside 600-650 ml for the parmigiana. Only then reserve whatever remains for another meal. If the sauce has reduced slightly too far, loosen it with a small splash of water before dividing. Season the reserved sauce separately to taste before cooling and storing. Keep the parmigiana portion a little restrained because cheese, sun-dried tomatoes and smoked salt are still to come; tear several basil leaves into this portion.

steps.title: Make the dark heart
steps.body: Take 120-140 ml from the parmigiana sauce. Add ⅛ tsp Halen Môn Oak Smoked Water, stir and taste. Add more only a few drops at a time — probably no more than about ¼ tsp in total. The target is tomato first, gentle oak smoke afterwards. If the first thing you taste is smoke, you have gone too far.

steps.title: Prepare the sun-dried tomatoes
steps.body: Drain 50-60 g sun-dried tomatoes and blot away excess oil. Cut into small strips or pieces and reserve 1 tsp of their oil. These belong only in the dark-heart layer.

steps.title: Base the dish
steps.body: Spread a very thin film — about 40-50 ml — of ordinary tomato sauce over the base of the baking dish.

steps.title: Layer 1 — Classic
steps.body: Aubergine, then 130-150 ml ordinary tomato sauce, about ¼ of the mozzarella, about ¼ of the hard cheese, torn basil and black pepper.

steps.title: Layer 2 — The Dark Heart
steps.body: Aubergine, then 120-140 ml smoked tomato sauce, all the sun-dried tomatoes, 1 tsp sun-dried tomato oil, about ¼ of the mozzarella, about ¼ of the hard cheese, torn basil and an optional tiny pinch of chilli.

steps.title: Layer 3 — Classic
steps.body: Aubergine, then 130-150 ml ordinary sauce, about ¼ of the mozzarella, about ¼ of the hard cheese, basil and black pepper.

steps.title: Layer 4 — Top
steps.body: Remaining aubergine, then 100-120 ml ordinary tomato sauce, the remaining hard cheese, the remaining mozzarella used sparingly, and 1 tsp EVOO.

steps.title: Bake
steps.body: Bake uncovered for 30-35 minutes. Look for bubbling edges, browned cheese, caramelised patches, melted mozzarella and no obvious watery pools. Give it another 5-10 minutes if required.

steps.title: Rest
steps.body: Leave completely undisturbed for 30-40 minutes. This is part of the cooking process: the layers settle, the aubergine absorbs sauce and the flavours become much clearer. Serve warm, not fiercely hot.

steps.title: Finish with the second smoke note
steps.body: Just before serving, crush 6-10 flakes of Maldon smoked sea salt between your fingers and scatter over the entire dish. Finish with fresh basil. Do not use the smoked salt as the general seasoning for the dish.

notes.label: Why it works
notes.body: The structure is deliberate: classic, then smoky centre, then classic, then browned savoury top. The smoke is not mixed through the whole dish. Halen Môn smoked water gives a subtle internal note; Maldon smoked sea salt gives occasional surface flashes. Sun-dried tomato deepens the centre without making the parmigiana taste heavily smoky or sweet.

notes.label: Smoke target
notes.body: If the first thing you taste is smoke, you have gone too far. The Halen Môn note should appear after the tomato, not before it. Keep both the smoked water and the sun-dried tomatoes to Layer 2 only.

notes.label: Cheese note
notes.body: For a strictly vegetarian dish, use vegetarian Italian-style hard cheese. If animal-rennet cheese is acceptable, Parmigiano Reggiano is the stronger flavour choice; add its rind to the simmering sauce if available.

notes.label: Key success points
notes.body: Drain the mozzarella thoroughly. Reduce the sauce until thick and spoonable, but protect the parmigiana allocation before reserving leftovers. Fry the aubergine until genuinely golden and tender, then drain very well. Keep the smoked water and sun-dried tomatoes to Layer 2. Use Maldon smoked salt only as a final accent. Give the baked parmigiana its full 30-40 minute rest.

notes.label: Serve with
notes.body: A bright, distinctly acidic fresh tomato salad alongside — ripe tomatoes, finely sliced red onion or shallot, basil, optional capers, dressed roughly 3 parts EVOO to 1 part red-wine vinegar or lemon juice. Serve it alongside rather than adding fresh tomato to the bake, so it refreshes the palate between bites.

notes.label: Using the spare sauce
notes.body: For pasta: reheat with a splash of pasta water and EVOO, adding fresh basil, black pepper and cheese at the table. For shakshuka: develop with cumin, paprika, chilli or harissa, with peppers or chickpeas, loosening slightly before adding the eggs.

notes.label: Make ahead, storage & reheating
notes.body: Bake earlier in the day, allow it to settle, then reheat gently before serving — parmigiana often improves after a few hours as the layers integrate. Cool promptly, cover and refrigerate for up to 3 days. Reheat at 160°C fan for about 20-25 minutes, loosely covered initially if already well browned. Add the Maldon smoked salt and fresh basil only after reheating. Spare sauce keeps around 3 days refrigerated, or freeze.
